summary: This sermon introduces a summer series on Paul's life by examining his early role as Saul the persecutor at Stephen's martyrdom in Acts 7-8. The message explores how Saul's religious certainty, intellectual pride, and self-righteousness as a Pharisee caused him to violently oppose the very Messiah he claimed to be waiting for, even as Stephen demonstrated Christ-like love by laying down his life.
key_points: Saul's identity as a Pharisee shaped his zealous persecution of the early church
Five Jewish responses to Roman occupation reveal different approaches to faithfulness
Stephen's martyrdom mirrored Jesus' crucifixion, yet Saul remained blind to the truth
Religious certainty and self-righteousness can cause us to miss God's actual work
We must respond to disagreement like Stephen (sacrificial love) not Saul (angry stubbornness)
big_idea: Our intellectual certainty and self-righteousness can blind us to who God truly is, causing us to fight against Him even while claiming to serve Him.
title: A SUMMER'S JOURNEY: The Sin of Religious Certainty
